summary: Drukpa Lama Rik Drol Gyatso studied under Patrul Rinpoche and Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo.

Active in Buddhist studies and Tibetology, Dudjom Jigdral Yeshe Dorje studied under Dza Pukhung Tulku Gyurme Ngedon Wangpo and Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö. He taught numerous students, including Sogyal Rinpoche and Keith Dowman.

Dudjom Rinpoche was a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Mindrolling and Dorje Drak monasteries under teachers including Sera Khandro and Khenpo Aten, founded the International Nyingma Society, and taught many students.

Indologist Dugald Mackichan studied at the University of Glasgow (M.A., B.D.) and the universities of Leipzig and Berlin. He served as Principal of Wilson College, Mumbai (1878–1920) and Vice-Chancellor of the University of Mumbai (1888–1890).

Duncan Forbes worked in linguistics and Indology after studying at Perth Grammar School and the University of St Andrews (M.A., LL.D.). He taught at Calcutta Academy, King's College London as Professor of Oriental languages, and the British Museum.

Duncan Ryūken Williams specializes in Buddhist, religious, and Japanese studies. After degrees at Reed College and Harvard University (Ph.D. under Masatoshi Nagatomi), he held posts at Harvard, UC Irvine, UC Berkeley, and the University of Southern California.
Dung Ngoc Duong is a scholar in Buddhist and religious studies who completed a PhD at Boston University by 2001 under the doctoral supervision of Malcolm David Eckel.

Dungkar Lobsang Thrinle worked in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. Educated at Trashichöling, Sera, and Gyuto monasteries, he held professorships at Minzu University of China and Tibet University, and served as Director of the Tibet Academy of Social Sciences.

Indologist Durga Mohan Bhattacharyya was educated at Vidyasagar College, Scottish Church College, and the University of Calcutta. He held professorships at Scottish Church College, Narasinha Dutt College, and the Sanskrit College and University.

Durga Prasad Dikshit worked in Indology and history and archaeology. He earned a PhD from the University of Lucknow under doctoral supervisor Baij Nath Puri, also studying under R. K. Dikshit and Vasudev Vishnu Mirashi.
Indologist Dušan Zbavitel studied at Charles University (1945–1949) under doctoral supervisor Vincenc Lesný, and later held an academic post at Charles University.

Dwarikadas Shastri worked in Indology and Buddhist studies. He earned a Bauddhadarśanācārya degree from Sampurnanand Sanskrit University, founded Bauddha Bharati, and served as joint editor at Nava Nalanda Mahavihara.

Specializing in religious studies and Japanology, Dwight Whitney Learned earned a B.A. and Ph.D. at Yale University under William Dwight Whitney. He taught at Thayer College before serving as Professor of Church History and Biblical Theology at Doshisha University.
Dwijendra Narayan Jha was a scholar in history, archaeology, and Indology. He completed his education at Presidency University, Patna University, and the University of Calcutta.

Scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies Dylan Esler earned a BA from SOAS and a PhD from KU Leuven. He has held research positions at KU Leuven, Ruhr University Bochum, and 84000: Translating the Words of the Buddha.

Active in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Tibetology, Dzigar Kongtrul Rinpoche studied under Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche, Tulku Urgyen Rinpoche, Nyoshul Khenpo Rinpoche, and Khenpo Rinchen. He founded Mangala Shri Bhuti and was professor of Buddhist philosophy at Naropa University.

Specializing in Buddhist studies and Tibetology, Dzogchen Ponlop Rinpoche studied at Karma Shri Nalanda Institute, Sampurnanand Sanskrit University, and Columbia University. He founded Nitartha International and Nalandabodhi, and served as director of Nitartha Institute and Kamalashila Institute.

Working in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and religious studies, Dzongsar Jamyang Khyentse Rinpoche studied at Sakya College and SOAS under Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche and Dudjom Rinpoche. He founded Siddhartha's Intent, Khyentse Foundation, and Deer Park Institute.
Working in Indology, linguistics, and history and archaeology, Dániel Balogh has held posts at the British Museum (attested 2021) and Eötvös Loránd University as a visiting lecturer (attested 2026).
Dávid Jónás specializes in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and Tibetology. He completed his PhD at Eötvös Loránd University in 2019, where he became an assistant lecturer in 2021.
